_comment: Copy to ./runconfig.json at the repo root and edit. Everything is optional;
omitted keys fall back to the built-in v1 roster and defaults in src/config.ts.
Pricing is USD per 1M tokens and is only used for the API-equivalent cost column —
subscription runs have no real per-run dollar figure (docs/PLAN.md).
_notion_comment: Live fixtures. Only consulted when `runtime: live` tasks are in the grid; an
offline run ignores this block entirely. Shape:
parentPageId is the page you shared with your Notion integration once. Every
per-trial fixture root is created under it and archived after that trial is
scored. Never use the workspace root: a workspace-level page cannot be archived
through the API, so a run would leak one un-deletable page per trial.
NOTION_PARENT_PAGE_ID and NOTION_API_BASE in the environment override these.
The integration TOKEN is deliberately absent and will stay absent — this file
gets checked in and pasted into issues. Set NOTION_API_TOKEN, or
NOTIONBENCH_NOTION_TOKENS=tok1,tok2 for a pool sized to --concurrency.
Left empty here so a copied config fails with `notionbench run`'s explicit
'set NOTION_PARENT_PAGE_ID' message rather than a 404 from a placeholder id.
_rateWindow_comment: Setting `patterns` REPLACES the built-in list in src/config.ts wholesale — it is
not merged — so copy the defaults you still want. The list below is the built-in
one, trimmed. The last three are OpenCode Go's usage-window wording, read out of
the English strings in the shipped opencode binary (1.18.10):
plus the structured reason:"account_rate_limit" that rides along with them.
These are unverified against a live throttled OpenCode run — no trial has hit the
window yet — so widen them if you see a phrasing they miss.

configs.label: Claude Code × Haiku 4.5 (budget)
configs.note: Budget config for the cost-Pareto story.

configs.label: OpenCode × Kimi K3
configs.note: First-class adapter (src/parsers/opencode.ts) — it owns the argv, including the --dir flag OpenCode needs to stay inside the trial workspace, and reads exact per-step token counts plus the provider-reported cost. Model is provider/model as OpenCode spells it. Kimi K3 on the Go plan is capped at 110 requests/5h, so schedule this lane first and let it trickle.

configs.label: Some other CLI (command template)
configs.note: Example of the generic harness: any prompt-in/files-out CLI. Placeholders are {prompt} {workspace} {model} {effort} {configId}; use promptVia:"stdin" for CLIs that read the prompt from stdin. Token accounting is heuristic (the tokens column reads "? tok" when nothing usage-shaped turns up) — write a dedicated adapter in src/parsers/ if the numbers must be exact, as claude-code, codex and opencode all do.
